newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moves in forex market may accelerate -- MOF adviser.
newsitem.headline: Moves in forex market may accelerate -- MOF adviser.

text.p: Japan needs to look at recent movements in currencies very carefully as there are signs that such movements may be about to accelerate, a special adviser to the finance minister said on Wednesday.
Kosuke Nakahira said in an interview with Reuters that excessive currency movements were not favourable for business activities, as such moves could lead to a loss of confidence in a currency.

"Recent currency movements warrant vigilance, as the market is reacting nervously to rumours and remarks by government officials," said Nakahira, a former vice finance minister for international affairs.
He said the dollar had risen against other major currencies, including the yen, and the recent movements were not a depreciation of the yen but rather an appreciation of the dollar.
"There are signs that recent currency movements may start accelerating,' he said.
He declined to say if he thought present currency movements required coordinated action by the Group of Seven (G7) nations to stabilise exchange rates.
"The main aim of the G7 is to normalise exchange rate movements when such movements deviate from economic fundamentals," he said.
He added that the currency market moved freely, with exchange rates determined by market forces, so it was not a good idea to talk about a specific range or level for a currency.
